title: The Role of U.S.-Based Professional Societies in Advancing and Creating Space for Global Psychological Science.
abstract: With growing recognition that psychological science has primarily focused on White Euro-American samples, constructs, theories, and methods, there is an urgent need to broaden the scope and inclusiveness of the discipline. Although journals, funding agencies, and individual scientists each play important roles in advancing this shift, U.S.-based professional societies are particularly well positioned to promote globally engaged psychological science. Recognizing this potential, the U.S. National Committee for Psychological Science, with assistance from the Federation of Associations in Behavioral and Brain Sciences, undertook an effort to gather and compile information about what U.S.-based professional societies are doing to enhance global engagement. Representatives of 24 professional societies across clinical, cognitive, developmental, and social psychology; statistics; behavioral medicine; neuroscience; and general psychology completed an online survey. Our analysis indicated that international focus was very important or important to more than 70% of the society representatives surveyed, and various activities to promote global engagement were described, although membership of Majority World scientists remained low, with limited integration of these scientists in leadership structures. On the basis of these findings and prior scholarship, we outline key approaches for inclusive, strategic, and scaffolded efforts to promote global psychological science.
